Data integration workflow

Source: vignettes/integration-workflow.Rmd
integration-workflow.Rmd

What you will do

  • Question: does correction reduce technology effects while retaining cell types?
  • Input: All 1,600 cells and 12,932 supplied genes in panc8_sub; tech identifies five technologies and celltype supplies evaluation labels.
  • Output: Uncorrected and Harmony reductions on the same cells, marker checks and a reloadable integrated object.
  • How to run: start a fresh R session and run the chunks in order. Printed tables and figures below are generated from that run; code-only alternatives are identified explicitly.

Use integration when technical structure prevents comparison across samples or platforms, and retain an unintegrated baseline. If every condition occurs in only one batch, batch and biology are confounded: no attractive embedding can resolve that experimental-design problem.

Prepare the required Harmony source

SCOP’s RunHarmony2() checks the official GitHub package origin. A CRAN installation with the same package name does not satisfy that check and can trigger an installation attempt in the middle of an analysis. Install the official GitHub source before starting this page, then restart R:

remotes::install_github(
  "immunogenomics/harmony",
  upgrade = "never"
)

The tutorial’s dependency preflight is read-only. It fails with a clear setup requirement instead of allowing an implicit installation during fitting.

Prepare a Merged Object

The example uses the bundled panc8_sub object, a subset of human pancreas datasets. The tech column records the batch or technology label. The celltype column is used as known biology for diagnostics, not as a target to force during integration.

library(scop)
set.seed(11)
harmony_source <- utils::packageDescription("harmony")
stopifnot(
  identical(harmony_source$RemoteUsername, "immunogenomics"),
  identical(harmony_source$RemoteRepo, "harmony")
)
data.frame(
  package = "harmony", version = harmony_source$Version,
  source = paste(harmony_source$RemoteUsername, harmony_source$RemoteRepo, sep = "/"),
  revision = harmony_source$RemoteSha
)
#>   package version                 source
#> 1 harmony   2.1.0 immunogenomics/harmony
#>                                   revision
#> 1 7e21bd6629b628099735395f57a47d11f873b2ee

data(panc8_sub)
input_cells <- colnames(panc8_sub)
stopifnot(!anyNA(panc8_sub$tech), !anyNA(panc8_sub$celltype))
data.frame(genes = nrow(panc8_sub), cells = ncol(panc8_sub))
#>   genes cells
#> 1 12932  1600
table(panc8_sub$tech)
#> 
#>     celseq    celseq2 fluidigmc1     indrop  smartseq2 
#>        200        200        200        800        200
table(panc8_sub$celltype)
#> 
#>             acinar activated-stellate              alpha               beta 
#>                164                 50                483                428 
#>              delta             ductal        endothelial            epsilon 
#>                111                237                 26                  3 
#>              gamma         macrophage               mast quiescent-stellate 
#>                 67                  9                  7                 14 
#>            schwann 
#>                  1

Always inspect the unintegrated embedding or PCA first. This gives you a baseline for deciding whether integration removes technical structure without erasing cell-type structure.

panc8_sub <- RunStandardWorkflow(panc8_sub,
  assay = "RNA", seed = 11, cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

CellDimPlot(
  panc8_sub,
  group.by = c("tech", "celltype"),
  reduction = "UMAP",
  theme_use = "theme_blank"
)

Run an Integration Method

Harmony is a common first pass when the object is already a merged Seurat object with a batch column.

panc8_harmony <- RunIntegration(
  srt_merge = panc8_sub,
  batch = "tech",
  integration_methods = "Harmony",
  nonlinear_reduction_dims = 2,
  seed = 11, verbose = FALSE
)
#> Warning: Different features in new layer data than already exists for
#> scale.data

stopifnot(identical(colnames(panc8_harmony), input_cells))
SeuratObject::Reductions(panc8_harmony)
#> [1] "Standardpca"       "StandardpcaUMAP2D" "StandardUMAP2D"   
#> [4] "Harmonypca"        "Harmony"           "HarmonyUMAP2D"    
#> [7] "HarmonypcaUMAP2D"

Use the method-specific integrated UMAP for plotting. The exact reduction name depends on the selected method; for Harmony, the examples use HarmonyUMAP2D. When comparing methods, report the reduction name explicitly. A plot labeled only as UMAP is ambiguous once an object contains uncorrected and integrated embeddings.

CellDimPlot(
  panc8_harmony,
  group.by = c("tech", "celltype"),
  reduction = "HarmonyUMAP2D",
  theme_use = "theme_blank"
)

Choose a Method

Use method choice to match the data and dependency budget:

  • Harmony, fastMNN, MNN, ComBat, and Seurat methods are practical R-side choices for many scRNA-seq batch problems.
  • scVI, BBKNN, Scanorama, GLUE, and MultiMAP require Python-side dependencies but can be useful for large datasets or multimodal settings.
  • WNN and cross-modality methods are better suited to multimodal RNA + ATAC or paired-modality objects than to ordinary batch correction.
  • Uncorrected is useful as a baseline and should be kept in reports when showing that integration changed the object.

The following alternatives are recipes, not additional measured results in this page. To compare executed methods, use the integration benchmark. Other methods follow the same entry-point pattern, but may require additional runtime dependencies or matrix backends:

panc8_rpca <- RunIntegration(
  srt_merge = panc8_sub,
  batch = "tech",
  integration_methods = "RPCA"
)

panc8_fastmnn <- RunIntegration(
  srt_merge = panc8_sub,
  batch = "tech",
  integration_methods = "fastMNN"
)

Inspect Integration Quality

Do not judge integration from batch mixing alone. Also check known labels, marker genes, and whether rare cell types remain separated.

CellDimPlot(
  panc8_harmony,
  group.by = "tech",
  reduction = "HarmonyUMAP2D",
  theme_use = "theme_blank"
)


CellDimPlot(
  panc8_harmony,
  group.by = "celltype",
  reduction = "HarmonyUMAP2D",
  label = TRUE,
  label_repel = TRUE, label.size = 3,
  theme_use = "theme_blank"
)


FeatureDimPlot(
  panc8_harmony,
  features = c("GCG", "SST", "KRT19"),
  reduction = "HarmonyUMAP2D"
)

When comparing methods, keep the input object fixed and compare the same metadata labels, marker genes, and diagnostic plots across methods. The unintegrated baseline is useful because it shows what the integration changed. Good integration mixes batches within the same biological state while keeping distinct cell types and marker programs separated. Overcorrection is visible when expected marker-defined groups collapse together.

INS is absent from the supplied feature-filtered object, so this marker check uses measured GCG, SST and KRT19. Missing input genes must not be interpreted as measured zero expression.

Save, reload, and check the hand-off

The code below saves to a temporary directory. Choose a persistent output folder when saving your analysis. Save the object and plain-text metadata; a figure alone cannot reproduce the analysis. No cells are sampled for this export.

output_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "integration-workflow")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
result_file <- file.path(output_dir, "analysis.rds")
saveRDS(panc8_harmony, result_file)
utils::write.csv(panc8_harmony@meta.data, file.path(output_dir, "cell-metadata.csv"))
reloaded <- readRDS(result_file)
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(reloaded), colnames(panc8_harmony)),
  identical(reloaded@meta.data, panc8_harmony@meta.data),
  identical(
    SeuratObject::Reductions(reloaded),
    SeuratObject::Reductions(panc8_harmony)
  )
)
data.frame(
  file = basename(list.files(output_dir, full.names = TRUE)),
  bytes = file.info(list.files(output_dir, full.names = TRUE))$size
)
#>                file    bytes
#> 1      analysis.rds 48007422
#> 2 cell-metadata.csv   186170

Use your own data and recover common errors

  • Replace the data(...) input with readRDS("your-object.rds"), or create a Seurat object from a gene-by-cell raw-count matrix. Check that cell IDs are unique and metadata row names equal the expression column names.
  • Set the assay and grouping columns explicitly. Species, gene identifiers and reference labels must match your experiment; do not copy pancreas labels to unrelated tissue.
  • If a reduction or metadata column is missing, inspect SeuratObject::Reductions(object) and colnames(object@meta.data), then run its producer chunk. A plot does not create the result it needs.
  • If a dependency is unavailable, install it in the analysis environment, restart R and rerun from the input chunk. A skipped or failed method is not evidence that it worked. Preserve warnings and the exact error in your report.

Analysis provenance

The receipt records the R seed. Python methods retain their documented backend seeds and parameters; setting the R seed alone does not control every backend. Package versions, BLAS libraries and backend changes can alter numerical results. Keep this receipt with the exported object.

source_revision <- Sys.getenv("GITHUB_SHA")
if (!nzchar(source_revision) && nzchar(Sys.which("git"))) {
  source_revision <- tryCatch(system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD"),
    stdout = TRUE,
    stderr = FALSE
  )[1], error = function(e) NA_character_)
}
article_source <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
build_receipt <- data.frame(
  article = "integration-workflow",
  built_utc = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE),
  scop = as.character(utils::packageVersion("scop")),
  R = as.character(getRversion()),
  source_revision = source_revision,
  source_has_local_changes = if (nzchar(Sys.which("git"))) {
    length(system2("git", c("status", "--porcelain"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)) > 0
  } else {
    NA
  },
  article_md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(article_source)),
  R_seed = 11,
  cells_retained = ncol(panc8_harmony),
  genes_in_active_assay = nrow(panc8_harmony),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
build_receipt
#>                article               built_utc  scop     R
#> 1 integration-workflow 2026-10-29 13:06:27 UTC 0.9.2 4.6.1
#>                            source_revision source_has_local_changes
#> 1 ad4b555307ddafe827a0748effa2efa29dc934c1                    FALSE
#>                        article_md5 R_seed cells_retained genes_in_active_assay
#> 1 258fa719de827f5739c0606e0dfd1e7c     11           1600                 12932
utils::write.csv(build_receipt, file.path(output_dir, "build-receipt.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt"))

What to Report

A compact integration report should include:

  • the batch column and biological annotation columns used for evaluation;
  • the integration method and major parameters;
  • the integrated reduction names used for plots;
  • before and after plots colored by batch and biological labels;
  • marker-gene checks for expected cell types;
  • any method-specific dependencies or environment setup needed to reproduce the run.

Integration is a preprocessing decision, not a biological result by itself. Use it only when the integrated representation improves downstream interpretation without hiding real biological differences.
